1. China produced about 36 per cent of the world's fish in 2022.
2. India is the second largest fish producer with about 8 per cent of world output.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
60.x: SOFIA 2024 puts China at 36%; India is second with about 8%.

60.s: The contribution of mulberry silk towards the world raw silk production is
60.x: Mulberry silk makes up the overwhelming bulk of world raw silk (about 90-95%), so 95 is the key; tasar, eri and muga are minor.

60.s: The leading mulberry silk producing Indian State is :
60.x: Karnataka leads mulberry silk (about half of India's); AP, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal follow.

60.s: Most common honey bee species in India
60.x: Apis indica (Apis cerana indica), the Indian hive bee, is the most common domesticated honey bee in India; A. dorsata is the wild rock bee, A. florea the little bee, A. mellifera the European bee.

60.s: The term ‘Kausheya’ has been used for
60.x: 'Kausheya' is the ancient Sanskrit term for silk (from kosha, the cocoon).

60.s: The country, which is the largest silk producer in the world, is :
60.x: China is the world's largest silk producer; India is second, notable as the only country producing all five commercial silks.

60.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
60.x: Karnataka is the leading state in mulberry silk. Jharkhand leads in tasar, while Assam leads in muga and eri silk.
60.tq: Discriminate among closely related state–product pairs.
xs: **Mulberry silk — Karnataka** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Tasar** = **Jharkhand**; **Muga** and **eri** = **Assam**.
xa: India is the **2nd largest silk producer** and the **only country** producing **all five silks**.
AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** (**61,394 MT** cocoons, 2024-25).

60.s: Through which body does the National Beekeeping and Honey Mission, launched in 2020, implement the Sweet Revolution?
60.x: The National Beekeeping and Honey Mission implements the Sweet Revolution through the National Bee Board.
xs: The **National Beekeeping and Honey Mission** runs the Sweet Revolution through the **National Bee Board** — option **(4)** is correct.
**NFDB** trains under PMMSY and **NDDB** launched Operation Flood — neither runs the honey mission.
xa: The mission was launched in **2020** under **Atmanirbhar Bharat**.
**Sweet Revolution** = honey (apiculture); **Golden Revolution (1991-2003)** = horticulture.
**NDDB** was set up in **1965** at **Anand, Gujarat**.

60.s: India is the only country producing all five commercial silks. Which of these is NOT among them?
60.x: The five commercial silks are mulberry, tropical tasar, oak tasar, eri and muga; Merino is not a silk.

60.s: Which of the following pairs of silk and leading State is correctly matched?
60.x: Tasar is led by Jharkhand, mulberry by Karnataka, and muga and eri by Assam.

60.s: India occupies which position in the production of silk, and what distinction is associated with its silk production?
o: First; it produces only one variety of silk
Second; it is the only country producing all five varieties of silk
Second; it produces only the mulberry variety
Third; it is the only country producing three varieties of silk
60.x: India is the second-largest silk producer and is identified as the only country producing all five varieties of silk.
60.tq: Combine the rank and the associated distinction instead of treating them as separate clues.
xs: India is the **second** largest silk producer and the **only country** producing **all five varieties of silk** — option **(2)** is correct.
The five: **mulberry**, **tropical tasar**, **oak tasar**, **eri**, **muga**.
xa: Mulberry = **Karnataka**; tasar = **Jharkhand**; muga & eri = **Assam**.
AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** (**61,394 MT** cocoons, 2024-25).

60.s: The Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for holistic growth of the horticulture sector, was implemented from which of the following years?
60.src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
60.x: MIDH is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2014-15; it subsumed the NHM (2005-06) and HMNEH.

60.s: When was the National Horticulture Mission started?
60.x: The National Horticulture Mission began in 2005-06 (launched May 2005) and was later subsumed in MIDH (2014-15).

60.s: Which of the following States is covered under the National Horticulture Mission (NHM) ?
60.x: NHM covered all States except the North-Eastern and Himalayan States (J&K, HP, Arunachal had HMNEH), so Uttar Pradesh is the NHM State.

60.s: Which one of the followings is not the objectives of 'National Horticulture Mission'?
60.x: NHM's objectives were higher growth in horticulture, post-harvest management and human resource development; financial assistance is only the means.

60.s: Where is the Indo-Israel Centre of Excellence for Vegetables and Flowers in Andhra Pradesh located?
60.x: The Indo-Israel Centre of Excellence for Vegetables and Flowers is at Kuppam, under MIDH and MASHAV.

60.s: MIDH subsumed which earlier mission launched in 2005-06?
60.x: MIDH (since 2014-15) subsumed the National Horticulture Mission (2005-06) and the NE/Himalayan horticulture mission.

60.s: Since which year has the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) been in operation?
60.x: MIDH, a Centrally Sponsored scheme, runs since 2014-15 and subsumed the National Horticulture Mission (2005-06).

60.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's horticulture sector?
o: It contributes about half of agricultural GVA
It exceeded foodgrain output of 357.73 million tonnes
It uses less than 14% of the cropped area
Its output in 2024-25 was 367.72 million tonnes
60.x: Horticulture contributes about 33% (one-third) of agricultural GVA, not half.
xa: Older 2026 notes put the GVA share at **30.4%**.
Top fruit by production: **banana**.
AP horticulture: **46.43 lakh acres**, **406.38 lakh MT** (AP Survey 2025-26).

60.s: Which allied agricultural sub-sector has recorded an annual growth rate of about 9.08% since 2014-15?
60.x: Fisheries has been the fastest-growing allied sub-sector, recording growth of about 9.08% annually since 2014-15.
60.tq: Associate the distinctive growth rate with the correct allied sector.
xs: **Fisheries** is the fastest-growing allied sub-sector at **9.08%** a year since **2014-15** — option **(2)** is correct.
ES 2025-26 puts the decadal rate (FY16-FY25) at **8.8%**.
xa: Output rose **103%**: **95.79 lakh t** (2013-14) → about **195 lakh t**.
**Inland fisheries** give over **75%** of output.
In AP, fishing & aquaculture is the largest allied sub-sector, growing **17.69%**.

60.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the growth of allied agricultural sectors in India?
o: Fisheries grew at a lower rate than livestock
60.x: Livestock grew at 7.1% and fisheries at 8.8%, so fisheries grew faster, not slower, than livestock.

60.s: In 2024-25, processed food products accounted for approximately what share of India's agricultural exports?
60.x: The APPSC-GS 2025 key used 'around 23%' as the share of processed food exports for 2024-25, so pick the option offered. 11.86% is a different figure: agri exports' share of merchandise exports.
60.tq: Separate two close percentage figures instead of treating them as interchangeable.
xs: The APPSC-GS 2025 key put processed food exports at "around **23%**" for 2024-25 — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: answer with the option offered; **11.86%** is a different figure — agri exports' share of merchandise exports.
xa: Agri exports (2024-25) hit a record **$51.9 billion**.
**MPEDA** (Kochi, under **Commerce**) is the apex body for marine-product exports.
60.fixed: stem referred to an answer key; reworded

60.s: In 2023-24, livestock accounted for about what share of India's agricultural GVA?
60.x: Livestock GVA was ₹15.06 lakh crore in 2023-24, about 30.87% of agri GVA.

60.s: India's agricultural exports reached a record of about how much in 2024-25?
60.x: Agri exports hit a record $51.9 billion in 2024-25, 11.86% of merchandise exports.

60.s: Horticulture contributes about what share of India's agricultural GVA?
60.x: Horticulture yields about 33% (one-third) of agri GVA on under 14% of the area, not half.

60.s: In 2024-25, India's horticulture output of 367.72 MT compared with foodgrains output how?
o: It was about half of foodgrains output
60.x: Horticulture output was 367.72 MT, more than foodgrains at 357.73 MT.

60.s: Which State is the largest producer of crude palm oil?
60.x: Andhra Pradesh leads India in oil palm area, production and productivity and produced 3.10 lakh MT of crude palm oil in 2023-24.

60.s: Which of the following pairs of mango varieties is associated with Andhra Pradesh’s exports?
60.x: Banganapalli and Totapuri are the mango varieties identified with Andhra Pradesh’s exports.
60.tq: Separate Andhra Pradesh export varieties from mango varieties associated with other regions.
xs: **Banganapalli** and **Totapuri** are the AP export mangoes — option **(1)** is correct.
**Alphonso** and **Kesar** are export varieties too, but not AP's.
xa: AP horticulture covers **46.43 lakh acres**, producing **406.38 lakh MT**.
**Rayalaseema** hub crops: banana, oil palm, cashew, coconut, **Araku coffee**.

60.s: Which State is the largest producer of fruits in India?
60.x: Andhra Pradesh leads India in fruit production; it also leads in shrimp, oil palm and eggs. Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka are not first in fruit.
60.tq: Identify the State rank and retain the associated national share.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** leads in fruit — option **(1)** is correct.
AP leads in **shrimp**, **fruit**, **oil palm** and **eggs**.
xa: AP is **1st** in eggs and oil palm, **2nd** in sheep and poultry numbers.
AP horticulture: **46.43 lakh acres**, **406.38 lakh MT**.
**Banana** is India's top fruit by production.

60.s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank among States in milk production?
60.x: AP is seventh in milk production (India is first); its principal national lead is in aquaculture.
xa: AP's milk fell **9.41%**; it was **5th** on 2022-23 figures.
India's milk share is about **25%** of world output; top State **UP (15.66%)**.

60.s: Which is the largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector in Andhra Pradesh?
60.x: Fisheries is AP's largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector, with 17.69% growth.
xa: AP gives about **29-30%** of India's fish output, mostly **Vannamei** shrimp.
NABARD 2026-27: **₹21,098 crore** to fisheries in AP.

60.s: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, how much area did horticulture cover in Andhra Pradesh?
60.x: The Survey reported horticulture over 46.43 lakh acres with production of 406.38 lakh MT.

60.s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank in coconut production?
60.x: Andhra Pradesh is 4th in coconut production. It is 1st in oil palm (2.27 lakh ha), so do not confuse the two rankings.
60.tq: Distinguish the coconut rank from the State’s first rank in oil palm and fruit production.
xs: AP is **4th in coconut** — option **(4) Fourth** is correct.
⚠ Do not confuse it with **oil palm**, where AP is **No. 1** (**2.27 lakh ha**).
xa: AP is **1st in eggs** but only **7th in milk**.
AP is **5th in meat** and **2nd** largest raw silk producer.

60.s:
Consider the following about Andhra Pradesh:
1. It is the largest producer of aquaculture and farmed shrimp in India.
2. Vannamei is its predominant farmed shrimp variety.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
60.x: AP is India's largest aquaculture and farmed-shrimp producer, and Vannamei is the predominant variety.
xa: AP fish output: **47.28 lakh t** up to Dec 2025 = **72%** of target.
NABARD 2026-27: **₹21,098 crore** to fisheries in AP.
⚠ India is **1st** in milk, but AP's lead is in **aquaculture**.

60.s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank among Indian States in raw silk production (2024-25)?
60.x: AP is the 2nd largest raw silk producer (61,394 MT of cocoons in 2024-25), with its belt around Hindupur (Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur) and Chittoor. India as a whole is also 2nd in the world. First, third and fifth are wrong.
60.tq: AP = 2nd in raw silk; India = 2nd in world silk.
xs: AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** — option **(2) Second** is correct.
It produced **61,394 MT** of cocoons in **2024-25**.
xa: AP's sericulture belt: **Sri Sathya Sai / Anantapur** around **Hindupur**, and **Chittoor**.
India too is the **2nd largest silk producer** in the world.
India is the only country producing **all five silks**.

60.s: Which of the following crops or products is NOT included among the horticultural activities identified for the development of Rayalaseema as a horticulture hub?
60.x: The identified activities include banana, oil palm, cashew, coconut and Araku coffee. Tea is not included in that list.
60.tq: Find the crop outside the stated regional horticulture cluster.
xs: **Tea** is not in the Rayalaseema hub list — option **(3)** is the answer.
The hub covers **banana**, **oil palm**, **cashew**, **coconut** and **Araku coffee**.
xa: **NABARD 2026-27** AP plan: **₹5,313 crore** for horticulture in Rayalaseema and Prakasam.
AP is **No. 1** in oil palm (**2.27 lakh ha**) and **4th** in coconut.
60.fixed: Araku coffee is from Araku Valley (ASR district, north coastal AP), not Rayalaseema

60.s: Which area forms the main sericulture belt of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur around Hindupur and Chittoor
60.x: The principal sericulture belt lies in Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur, particularly around Hindupur, and in Chittoor.
60.tq: Identify the precise geographical concentration from a set of nearby districts.
xs: AP's sericulture belt is **Sri Sathya Sai / Anantapur** around **Hindupur**, and **Chittoor** — option **(2)** is correct.
These Rayalaseema districts are named as AP's sericulture belt.
xa: AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** (**61,394 MT** cocoons, 2024-25).
**Chittoor** is also AP's top dairy district.
⚠ Mulberry = **Karnataka**; tasar = **Jharkhand**; muga & eri = **Assam**.

60.s: At what rate did fishing and aquaculture, Andhra Pradesh's largest allied sub-sector, grow?
60.x: Fishing and aquaculture is AP's largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector at 17.69%.

60.s: For which crop is Araku Valley in Andhra Pradesh known?
60.x: Araku is known for coffee, not tea.

60.s: In which of the following does Andhra Pradesh rank first in India?
60.x: AP is 1st in oil palm (2.27 lakh ha); it is 7th in milk, 4th in coconut and 2nd in raw silk.

60.s: Which district is the top dairy district of Andhra Pradesh?
60.x: Chittoor is AP's top dairy district.

60.s: From which place are Andhra Pradesh's banana exports to the Gulf sent by refrigerated trains?
60.x: About 32,000 MT of bananas went to the Gulf by 8 refrigerated trains from Tadipatri.

60.s:
Assertion (A): Andhra Pradesh is the largest producer of farmed shrimp in India.
Reason (R): Vannamei is the predominant farmed shrimp of Andhra Pradesh.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
60.x: AP is the largest producer of aquaculture and farmed shrimp and Vannamei dominates its farms, but the species does not explain the rank.

60.s: Optimum age for vaccination in calves against brucellosis
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Female calves are vaccinated against brucellosis (S19 / RB51) once, at about 4-8 months – '4-6 months' among the options. (Off-topic: moved to animal husbandry.)

60.s: The production of horticulture crops has outpaced the production of food grains since
60.x: India's horticulture production has exceeded foodgrain production since 2012-13.

60.s: Dressing percentage is highest in
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Pigs have the highest dressing percentage (about 70-80%), well above cattle, sheep and goats (about 45-55%).

60.s: Collecting semen from male chicken is called
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Semen is collected from cocks by abdominal massage, called 'milking'; candling checks eggs, brooding rears chicks.

60.s: Which of the following animals is treated as a 'small ruminant' for development financial assistance schemes?
60.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
60.x: Sheep and goats are small ruminants; cows and buffaloes are large ruminants and ducks are poultry.

60.s: 'White Revolution' refers to
60.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
60.x: White Revolution = milk (Operation Flood); fish is Blue, eggs Silver, pearls not a 'revolution'.

60.s: The common method of identification of sheep and goat is
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Sheep and goats are commonly identified by ear tags (also ear notching); hot-iron branding is used for cattle.

60.s: Which of the following is more prolific meat animal
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Rabbits are the most prolific meat animals (short gestation, large litters).

60.s: Maximization of production of eggs is called:
60.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
60.x: Silver Revolution = maximum egg (poultry) production.

60.s: What is the position of India amongst the countries of World in terms of Production of eggs?
60.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
60.x:
India was 3rd (after China and the USA) when older keys were set — now 2nd in world egg production (DAHD BAHS 2024)
India is now the 2nd largest egg producer in the world after China (142.77 billion eggs, 2023-24); older books and keys gave 3rd (after China and the USA).

60.s: How much concentrate mixture is given for every one litre of cow milk over and above the maintenance
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Feeding standard: a dairy cow gets about 0.4 kg of concentrate per litre of milk (1 kg per 2.5 litres) over maintenance; a buffalo about 0.5 kg per litre.

60.s: Ideal market weight of pigs at slaughter
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Pigs are marketed at about 80-90 kg live weight (6-8 months), the weight at which feed efficiency and carcass quality are best.

60.s: In which of the following years, the National Food Processing Policy was formulated?
60.x: The draft National Food Processing Policy came in 2005 (with the Vision, Strategy and Action Plan for food processing); 2002-2004 are wrong. Agro-processing item, moved.

60.s: Feeding of excess proteins to Ruminants causes
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Excess protein in a ruminant's diet is broken down to ammonia in the rumen, raising its pH and causing alkaline indigestion. Acid indigestion follows excess grain (carbohydrate).

60.s:
Consider the following statements with respect to 'Gram Samridhi Yojana'.

a. Gram Samridhi Yojana, is a Rs. 3,000 crore scheme funded by the World Bank and the Government of India, to strengthen the unorganised food processing sector concentrated in rural areas.

b. World Bank will be giving Rs. 1,000 crore, Rs. 1,500 crore will be borne by the Centre while state governments will put in Rs. 500 crore.

c. The scheme will be run in Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Punjab for a 5-year period.
Which of the above statement is incorrect?
60.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
60.x: As keyed, statement b on the funding split of the Gram Samridhi Yojana is the incorrect one.

60.s: After Reorganization, the "Vijaya" milk brand belongs to?
60.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
60.x: After bifurcation both States' dairy federations use the 'Vijaya' brand (Telangana as 'Vijaya Telangana') and the ownership is still disputed, so neither 'Telangana' nor 'AP' alone is right. Off-topic (dairy), moved.

60.s: Turning of the eggs should be done during the incubation period in chicken
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Eggs are turned from day 1 to day 18 of the 21-day chicken incubation; turning stops in the last three days (hatching period).

60.s: The most widely used extender for frozen semen is
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Tris (tris-egg yolk-citrate-glycerol) is the most widely used extender for frozen bull semen.

60.s: India is ranked first in milk production in the world in 2015-16 with the production accounting for following percentage of world production?
60.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
60.x: In 2015-16 India produced about 155.5 million tonnes of milk, roughly 18.5% of world production, and ranked first. 50% and 30% are far too high.

60.s: Which of the following is NOT considered an Indian Major Carp?
60.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
60.x: The Indian major carps are rohu, catla and mrigal. Tilapia (Oreochromis mossambicus) is an exotic African cichlid. (Off-topic: fisheries.)

60.s: The percentage of CO2 in an egg incubator for achieving optimum hatchability
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Optimum hatchability needs CO2 kept low, about 0.3-0.5% in the incubator; higher levels cut hatchability.

60.s: The primary purpose of vaccinating animals is
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Vaccination of animals primarily prevents infectious diseases; it does not treat animals or prevent non-infectious diseases.

60.s: What is the moisture percent present in hay
60.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
60.x: Well-cured hay keeps about 15-18% moisture. Wetter hay moulds. (Off-topic: animal husbandry.)

60.s: Kanva-2, S-36, S-14 and S-54 are hybrid varieties of
60.x: Kanva-2, S-36, S-54 and similar are high-yielding mulberry varieties bred for sericulture (CSRTI Mysore). (Off-topic: sericulture.)

60.s: Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme for genetic upgradation of Bovines in the country is being implemented under which scheme?
60.x: The Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme for genetic upgradation of bovines is implemented under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission.

60.s: With which period is the Golden Revolution in India associated?
60.x: The horticulture boom during 1991–2003 is known as the Golden Revolution.
60.tq: Associate the named revolution with its stated time span.
xs: The **Golden Revolution** (horticulture boom) covers **1991-2003** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Golden Revolution** = horticulture, but **Golden Fibre** = **jute**.
xa: **Silver Fibre** = cotton; **Sweet Revolution** = honey; **Blue** = fisheries; **White** = milk.
**MIDH** (since **2014-15**) is today's horticulture scheme.

60.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its revolution or fibre designation?
60.x: The Sweet Revolution is associated with honey and apiculture. Golden Fibre denotes jute, Silver Fibre denotes cotton, and Blue Revolution denotes fisheries.
60.tq: Separate similar revolution names from fibre designations.
xs: **Sweet Revolution — honey** (apiculture) is correctly matched — option **(2)**.
**Golden Fibre** = **jute**; **Silver Fibre** = **cotton**; **Blue** = **fisheries** (milk is **White**).
xa: The **National Beekeeping and Honey Mission (2020)** runs the Sweet Revolution via the **National Bee Board**.
**Golden Revolution (1991-2003)** = horticulture.

60.s: With which product is the Yellow Revolution in India associated?
60.x: The Yellow Revolution relates to oilseeds; Silver is eggs, Sweet is honey and Round is potato.

60.s: Which fibre is called Silver Fibre?
60.x: Silver Fibre is cotton and Golden Fibre is jute; Silver Revolution is eggs.

60.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
60.x: Grey Revolution relates to fertilisers; Round is potato, Pink is meat and poultry, Sweet is honey.

60.s: Which revolution is the umbrella term covering all farm and allied sectors?
60.x: The Rainbow Revolution is the umbrella term for all farm and allied sectors.

60.s: Who is associated with the Yellow Revolution in oilseeds?
60.x: The Yellow Revolution in oilseeds is linked with Sam Pitroda.

60.s: Who is associated with the Green Revolution in India?
60.x: M.S. Swaminathan is called the father of the Green Revolution in foodgrains.

60.s: With which products is the Pink Revolution associated?
60.x: The Pink Revolution relates to meat and poultry (also onion); eggs are the Silver Revolution.

61.s:

Select the correct answer using the code given below:

61.s:

61.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. NTPC is the largest power utility in India

2. ONGC accounts for half of the LPG production in India

3. Indian Oil Corporation operates all the oil refineries in India

4. The Indian Ordnance Factory is the largest departmentally run industrial undertaking in the country

61.x: NTPC is the largest power utility and the Ordnance Factories the largest departmental undertaking, so 1 and 4; ONGC does not make half the LPG and IOC does not run all refineries.

61.s: The top profit making enterprise of the Government of India is
61.x: ONGC was the top profit-making Government enterprise, ahead of SAIL and MTNL.

61.s: The following Emblem indicates (an eye logo):

61.s: Which of the following Public Sector Undertakings are not contributing to profits and are running on losses?
o: Hindustan Fertilizers and Chemicals Corporation of India
VSNL and Food Corporation of India
61.x: Hindustan Fertilizers and Chemicals Corporation was a chronic loss-maker; VSNL, FCI, NTPC, IOC, ONGC and BCCL pairs include profit-making units.

61.s: Which one of the following is not of the same category :
61.x: Essar Oil (now Nayara Energy) is a private company, while SAIL, BHEL and ONGC are public sector undertakings.

61.s: In which one of the following Public Sector Enterprises the Government has 100% equity ?
61.x: BSNL is 100% owned by the Government of India; NTPC, BHEL and SBI have public shareholders.

61.s: Which Central Public Enterprise has borne loss in India in the year 2014-15?
61.x: BSNL was a loss-making CPSE in 2014-15; ONGC, NMDC and Coal India made profits.

61.s: The Oil and Natural Gas Commission (ONGC) was set up in :
61.x: The Oil and Natural Gas Commission was set up on 14 August 1956 (made statutory in 1959).

61.s: Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd., Bhopal was established with the support of a company of which country?

61.x: The segments are mill, powerloom and handloom; powerlooms make most cloth.

The services counterpart of the IIP

61.s:

61.s: In India, which state has the highest capital intensity in manufacturing sector in 2017-18?

61.s: How many industries were reserved for the public sector under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, and how many were retained under the 1991 policy?

61.tq: Compare the two policy benchmarks and watch for reversal of the figures.
xs: **IPR 1956** reserved **17** industries for the public sector; the **1991 policy** cut this to **8** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the two numbers.

61.s: Besides wars, droughts and licensing, which of the following caused India's industrial deceleration during 1965-80?
61.x: Wars, droughts, infrastructure bottlenecks and licensing caused the 1965-80 slowdown; import liberalisation was not a feature of that period.

61.s: What did the Second Five Year Plan, based on the Mahalanobis model, emphasise?
61.x: The Second Plan and the Mahalanobis model stressed basic and heavy industries.

**IPR 1956** reserved **17** industries for the public sector.

61.s: What does the concept of premature deindustrialisation, associated with Dani Rodrik, mean?
o: manufacturing's share peaks at a lower income level than in early industrialising countries
industrial employment rises continuously after reaching high income
services remain smaller than agriculture at every income level
61.x: Premature deindustrialisation occurs when manufacturing's share of output or employment peaks at a lower income level than it did in early industrialisers.
61.tq: Distinguish a lower-income peak from the complete disappearance of manufacturing.
xs: **Premature deindustrialisation** (**Dani Rodrik**): **manufacturing**'s share **peaks** at a **lower income** than in early industrialisers — option **(1)** is correct.
It does not mean manufacturing vanishes or that employment keeps rising.
xa: After 1991, **cheap imports** shut many small units.
**Services**, not industry, gained most GDP share after 1991.

61.s: What was India's approximate industrial growth rate during the 1965-80 phase of deceleration?
61.x: Growth fell to about 4% in 1965-80, against about 7-8% in 1951-65 and in the 1980s.
xa: The 1965-80 slowdown came from **wars**, **droughts**, **infrastructure bottlenecks** and **licensing**.
**Dani Rodrik**'s **premature deindustrialisation**: manufacturing peaks at lower income than in early industrialisers.

61.s: What was India's approximate industrial growth rate during the public-sector-led phase of 1951-65?
61.x: The 1951-65 phase of heavy industrialisation grew about 7-8%, against about 4% in 1965-80.

61.s: Industry accounts for approximately what share of Gross Value Added in India?
61.x: Industry accounts for approximately 25.3 per cent of GVA. The 13–14 per cent figure relates to the public sector's contribution to GDP, while 17–18 per cent refers to manufacturing's real-term share.
61.tq: Separate similar percentages by linking each figure to its correct economic aggregate.
xs: Industry is about **25.3 per cent** of GVA — option **(4)** is correct.
**13-14%** is the public sector's share of GDP; **17-18%** is manufacturing's real share.
xa: Real industry GVA grows at about **7%**.
Industry GVA grew **7.0%** in H1 FY26.

61.s:
Consider the following about India's sectoral GDP structure after 1991:

61.s: Why did manufacturing's share of nominal GVA decline despite its real-term share remaining broadly stable?
o: Because the private sector withdrew from manufacturing
Because construction was excluded from GVA
Because manufacturing output ceased to grow after 1991
61.x: The decline in manufacturing's nominal GVA share was attributed to relative price changes. In real terms, manufacturing's share remained broadly steady at 17–18 per cent.
61.tq: Distinguish nominal changes caused by prices from real changes in output.
xs: Manufacturing's **nominal** GVA share fell only because of **relative price** changes — option **(1)** is correct.
Its **real** share stayed steady at **17-18%**, so output did not stop growing.
xa: Manufacturing GVA grew **9.13%** in Q2 FY26.
Industry as a whole is about **25.3%** of GVA.

61.s: The public sector accounts for about what share of India's GDP?
61.x: The public sector is about 13-14% of GDP, so the private sector dominates industrial output.

61.s: Medium- and high-tech manufacturing accounts for about what share as per the Economic Survey 2025-26?

61.x: Manufacturing's real share is steady at 17-18%; its nominal share fell only due to relative prices.

61.s: Industrial concentration in India is particularly pronounced in which group of States?

PSU townships such as **Bhilai, Rourkela, Bokaro** were meant for regional balance.

61.s: Which of the following shows 'jobless growth' in Indian factories during 2011-2023?
o: Direct factory employment rose from 47% to 61% of the workforce
The share of directly employed workers fell from 61% to 47%, and contract workers now make up about 42%
Contract workers fell to about 4% of the factory workforce
Factory employment grew faster than factory output
61.x: Directly employed workers fell from 61% to 47% of the factory workforce (2011-2023), and contract workers now make up about 42%. Option A reverses the trend, C understates contract labour, and D is the opposite of jobless growth.
xs: **Jobless growth**: direct factory employment fell from **61%** to **47%** (**2011-2023**); contract workers are now about **42%** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the trend; (3) understates contract labour.
xa: Regular CPSE employment fell by **30,000** in **2024**, replaced by contract workers.
About **57 lakh** jobs were added in organised manufacturing (2015-16 to 2024-25).

61.s: What is the principal cause of capacity under-utilisation in Indian industry?
61.x: Deficient basic infrastructure is identified as the main cause of capacity under-utilisation, although weak demand also contributes.

xs: The main cause of capacity under-utilisation is **deficient basic infrastructure** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2007).
**Weak demand** also adds: the Manufacturing PMI in **Jul 2026** was the lowest since **Aug 2021**.
xa: Other problems: **regional concentration**, **jobless growth**, **import dependence**, **low R&D**.

61.s: The expression 'commanding heights' in the context of India's public sector primarily refers to control over which of the following?

62.x: KVIC is a statutory body under the Ministry of MSME; the other statements are correct.

62.s: Under which Ministry does the National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) function?
o: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
62.x: NSIC is a public enterprise under the Ministry of MSME that helps market small industry products.

62.s: In which year was the National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) set up?
62.x: NSIC was set up by the Government of India in 1955; it works under the Ministry of MSME.

62.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: TReDS – Offline cash-payment system for MSME invoices
SIDBI – Implementing agency for PM SVANidhi
CGTMSE – Co-founded by SIDBI and NABARD
62.x: SIDBI implements PM SVANidhi; TReDS is an online invoice-discounting system, CGTMSE was co-founded with the Ministry of MSME and SIDBI is at Lucknow.

62.s: In which year did SIDBI co-found the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)?
62.x: CGTMSE was co-founded by the Ministry of MSME and SIDBI in 2000 to provide credit guarantee support for collateral-free lending.
62.tq: Distinguish the year of SIDBI’s establishment from the later year of CGTMSE’s formation.
xs: **CGTMSE** was set up in **2000** by the **Ministry of MSME** and **SIDBI** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1990** is SIDBI's own founding year.
xa: It gives **collateral-free credit guarantee** cover to lenders.
Its corpus is shared **Government : SIDBI = 4:1**.

62.s: Which body regulates TReDS platforms such as RXIL, M1xchange and Invoicemart, which discount MSME receivables?
62.x: TReDS platforms are RBI-regulated and discount MSME receivables owed by corporates, government and PSUs.
xa: TReDS has run since **2017**.
Budget **2026-27**: **all CPSE purchases from MSMEs** to settle on TReDS, plus a **GeM-TReDS** link.

62.s:
Consider the following about the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS):
1. It is an RBI platform for discounting receivables.
2. It was a Covid-era emergency credit scheme introduced in 2020.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
62.x: ECLGS was the Covid-era (2020) emergency credit-guarantee line for MSMEs; the receivables-discounting platform is TReDS.
xa: **ECLGS 5.0** (**May 2026**) gives a **100%** guarantee to units hit by the **West Asia crisis**.
**Udyam Registration** also began in **2020**.

62.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two loan limits stated for MSE lending in February 2026?
o: No collateral is required up to ₹25 lakh, while banks may lend only up to ₹20 lakh.
No collateral is required up to ₹20 lakh, while banks may extend the limit up to ₹25 lakh.
Both limits are fixed at ₹20 lakh.
Both limits are fixed at ₹25 lakh.
62.x: The stated position is a ₹20 lakh no-collateral threshold, with banks permitted to go up to ₹25 lakh.
62.tq: Separate two closely related numerical limits instead of treating them as identical.
xs: RBI (**Feb 2026**): **no collateral** for MSE loans up to **₹20 lakh**, and banks may go up to **₹25 lakh** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) swaps the two limits.
xa: **MUDRA** loans are also collateral-free up to **₹20 lakh**.
**CGTMSE** backs collateral-free lending with a **4:1** Government:SIDBI corpus.

62.s: With reference to TReDS, Budget 2026-27 announced which of the following?
o: TReDS platforms will be regulated by SEBI instead of the RBI
All CPSE purchases from MSMEs are to be settled on TReDS, with CGTMSE guarantees for TReDS discounting
TReDS will be merged with the MSME Samadhaan portal
Only private corporates will be allowed to use TReDS
62.x: Budget 2026-27 mandated settlement of all CPSE purchases from MSMEs on TReDS, CGTMSE guarantees for TReDS discounting, a GeM-TReDS link and receivables as asset-backed securities. TReDS platforms remain RBI-regulated, are not merged with Samadhaan (a delayed-payment portal), and serve government and PSU buyers as well as corporates.
62.tq: Budget 2026-27: CPSE-MSME bills via TReDS + CGTMSE cover + GeM link.
xs: Budget 2026-27 said **all CPSE purchases from MSMEs** are to be settled on **TReDS**, with **CGTMSE guarantees for TReDS discounting** — so option **(2)** is correct.
TReDS platforms are **RBI-regulated** (since **2017**), not SEBI-regulated.
**MSME Samadhaan** (2017) is a separate delayed-payment portal; TReDS also serves **government and PSU** buyers, not only private corporates.
xa: The Budget also proposed a **GeM-TReDS link** and treating receivables as **asset-backed securities**.
TReDS platforms include **RXIL**, **M1xchange** and **Invoicemart**.
**GeM:** **Rs 18.4 lakh crore** GMV with **11 lakh+** MSEs (Aug 2026).

62.s: Under PMMY (MUDRA), up to what amount are collateral-free loans available?
62.x: MUDRA gives collateral-free loans up to ₹20 lakh under Shishu, Kishor, Tarun and Tarun Plus.

62.s: ECLGS 5.0 (May 2026) gives a 100% guarantee to units hit by which of the following?
62.x: ECLGS 5.0 (May 2026) offers 100% guarantee for units hit by the West Asia crisis; ECLGS itself began in 2020.

62.s:
Consider the following statements about CGTMSE:
1. It provides collateral-free credit guarantees.
2. Its corpus is shared between the Government and SIDBI in the ratio 1:4.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
62.x: CGTMSE gives collateral-free guarantees; its corpus ratio is Government : SIDBI = 4:1, not 1:4.

62.s: Which of the following is NOT a loan category under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana?
62.x: MUDRA loans are given as Shishu, Kishor, Tarun and Tarun Plus; there is no Vriddhi category.

62.s: What is the full form of MUDRA?
o: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency
Micro Units Development and Regulatory Authority
Medium Units Development and Refinance Agency
Micro Undertakings Delivery and Refinance Agency
62.x: MUDRA stands for Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency; it refinances loans to micro units.

62.s: In which year did the TReDS platforms for discounting MSME invoices start?
62.x: TReDS, the RBI-regulated online invoice discounting system (RXIL, M1xchange, Invoicemart), started in 2017.

62.s: MUDRA was set up as a wholly owned subsidiary of which institution?
62.x: MUDRA was set up in 2015 as a wholly owned subsidiary of SIDBI to refinance loans to micro units.

62.s: When was the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana launched?
62.x: PMMY and MUDRA were launched by the Prime Minister on 8 April 2015.

62.s: What is the corpus contribution ratio between the Government and SIDBI in CGTMSE?
62.x: The corpus of CGTMSE is shared between the Government and SIDBI in the ratio of 4:1.
62.tq: Recall the exact institutional contribution ratio rather than the scheme’s broad objective.
xs: The CGTMSE corpus is shared **Government : SIDBI = 4:1** — option **(1)** is correct.
CGTMSE was set up in **2000**.
xa: Budget **2026-27** adds **CGTMSE** guarantees for **TReDS** discounting.
**MUDRA** ceiling: **₹20 lakh** (**Tarun Plus**).

62.s: Small enterprises refer to those units which have got gross fixed capital of
62.x:
Most keys: Rs 5 lakh (the 1950 'gross fixed capital' definition). Strictly: at the 1983-84 exam the limit was Rs 20 lakh in plant and machinery (1980 policy) (app notes 3:62).
Small units were first defined (1950) by gross fixed capital up to Rs 5 lakh, the answer keys give. Strictly, by 1983 the limit was Rs 20 lakh in plant and machinery.

62.s: In 1950, an enterprise which invested a maximum of ____ was classified as a 'small-scale industrial unit' in India.
62.x: In 1950 a small-scale unit was one with investment (gross fixed capital) up to Rs 5 lakh.

62.s:
Consider the following statements with reference to India :

a. According to the 'Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006', the 'medium enterprises' are those with investments in plant and machinery between ₹ 15 crore and ₹ 25 crore.

b. All bank loans to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises qualify under the priority sector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
62.x: Statement a is wrong: a medium enterprise may invest up to Rs 50 crore (2020; now Rs 125 crore), not Rs 15-25 crore. Statement b is right: all bank loans to MSMEs qualify as priority sector.

62.s: In which of the following year, the latest classification of MSME was done?
62.x:
the limits were raised again from 1 April 2025 (Budget 2025-26) — now the latest classification is 2025 (app notes 3:62)
The latest MSME classification at the 2021 exam was the 2020 composite investment-plus-turnover one (now revised again, from 1 April 2025).

62.s: The limit of capital investment for small scale industries as per New Industrial Policy, 1991 is :
62.x: The 1991 Industrial Policy raised the small-unit investment limit from Rs 35 lakh to Rs 60 lakh.

62.s: Foreign equity holding allowed in small scale sector in 1995-96 is :
62.x: Foreign (and other-industry) equity in a small-scale unit was capped at 24% in 1995-96.

62.s: Small scale enterprise is defined on the basis of which of the following parameters?
o: Number of workers in the Enterprise
Investment in the plant and machinery and equipment of the Enterprise
Investment in plant and machinery and equipment as well as annual turnover of the Enterprise
62.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
62.x: Since 2020 an enterprise is classed by investment in plant and machinery/equipment AND annual turnover.

62.s: What is the current investment limit in Small Scale Industry?
62.x: In 2004 the SSI investment limit was Rs 1 crore (100 lakh), set in 1999.

62.s:
Consider the following factors regarding an industry :
1. Capital investment
2. Business turnover
3. Labour force
4. Power consumption Which of these determine the nature and size of the industry?
62.x:
Official key: 1, 3 and 4. Strictly: turnover is also used today (MSMEs since 2020), so 2 is arguable (app notes 3:62).
Capital investment, labour force and power consumption are taken (official key) to decide the nature and size of an industry; turnover is also relevant.

62.s: Which of the following partly defines the micro-enterprise in India?
o: Investment in Plant and Machinery or equipment not
Annual turnover not more than Rs. 15 crore
Investment in Plant and Machinery not more than Rs
Annual turnover of more than Rs. 5 crore
Annual turnover not more than Rs. 5 crore
62.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Annual turnover not more than Rs. 5 crore); it is added as option 5.
micro turnover ceiling Rs 5 crore (2020) — now Rs 10 crore from 1 April 2025 (app notes 3:62)
Under the 2020 criteria a micro enterprise has investment up to Rs 1 crore and turnover up to Rs 5 crore (now Rs 2.5 crore / Rs 10 crore). The printed 'turnover not more than Rs 15 crore' was never a limit, the investment options are cut off in the source, and 'more than Rs 5 crore' is wrong.

62.s: Investment in Plant and Machinery in a small scale manufacturing unit should be :
o: Above Rs. 10 lakh but not more than Rs. 25 lakh
Above Rs. 25 lakhs but not more than Rs. 5 crore
Above Rs. 5 crore but not more than Rs.10 crore
62.x:
2006 limit Rs 25 lakh-5 crore — now small = investment up to Rs 25 crore and turnover up to Rs 100 crore (from 1 April 2025) (app notes 3:62)
Under the MSMED Act 2006 a small manufacturing unit invested above Rs 25 lakh and up to Rs 5 crore in plant and machinery (now up to Rs 25 crore with turnover up to Rs 100 crore).

62.s: Which is not included in manufacturing sector?
62.x: Under the MSMED Act manufacturing units are micro, small, medium (or large); 'small scale industry' is the old pre-2006 category, which is why it is the odd one out.

62.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the evolution of MSME classification?
o: In 1950, a small-scale unit had an investment ceiling of ₹5 lakh.
The Industrial Policy of 1991 raised the investment ceiling for SSI units.
The 2006 framework prescribed separate limits for manufacturing and services.
The composite investment-and-turnover criterion was notified on 1 June 2010.
62.x: The composite investment-and-turnover criterion was notified on 1 June 2020, not 2010. The other three milestones are correct.
xa: The 2020 change came with the **Aatmanirbhar** package and dropped the manufacturing/services distinction.
Limits were revised again from **1 April 2025** (Budget 2025-26).
The 1950 ₹5 lakh ceiling was asked in **APPSC-GS 2022**.

62.s: When did the MSMED Act, 2006 come into force?
62.x: The MSMED Act, 2006 came into force on 2 October 2006. Its Bill had been introduced on 12 May 2005.
62.tq: Distinguish the date of introduction of the Bill from the date on which the Act came into force.
xs: The **MSMED Act, 2006** came into force on **2 October 2006** — option **(1)** is correct.
**12 May 2005** is when the **SME Development Bill** was introduced; **1 June 2020** is the composite-criterion notification.
xa: Chapter V: buyers must pay within **45 days**, else compound interest at **3 times** the **RBI bank rate**.
Disputes go to the **MSE Facilitation Council**.

62.s:
Under the original MSMED definitions of 2006:
1. A small manufacturing enterprise could invest up to ₹5 crore in plant and machinery.
2. The corresponding limit for a small service enterprise was ₹2 crore.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
62.x: The 2006 limit for small manufacturing was ₹5 crore in plant and machinery, and for small services ₹2 crore.
xa: Micro manufacturing: up to **₹25 lakh**.
Medium services: up to **₹5 crore**.

62.s: In 1950, what was the investment limit for a small-scale unit?
62.x: The 1950 definition set the small-scale investment limit at ₹5 lakh.

62.s: Under the original MSMED Act, 2006, up to what amount could a micro service enterprise invest in equipment?
62.x: In 2006, micro service units could invest up to ₹10 lakh; micro manufacturing up to ₹25 lakh.

62.s: When was the composite investment-plus-turnover criterion for MSMEs notified?
62.x: The composite criterion was notified on 1 June 2020 (effective 1 July 2020); 13 May 2020 was the announcement.

62.s: To what level did the Industrial Policy of 1991 raise the investment limit for a small-scale unit?
62.x: The 1991 policy raised the small-unit limit from ₹35 lakh to ₹60 lakh (ancillary ₹75 lakh).

62.s: What was the investment limit for a small-scale unit in 2004, before the MSMED Act?
62.x: The SSI limit was cut from ₹3 crore (1997) to ₹1 crore (1999), and stayed so in 2004.

62.s: To what level did the Industrial Policy of 1991 raise the investment limit for ancillary units?
62.x: The 1991 policy raised the ancillary limit from ₹45 lakh to ₹75 lakh (small units ₹35 lakh to ₹60 lakh).

62.s: Since the 2020 notification, the classification of an MSME is based on which of the following?
o: Investment in land and number of employees
Investment in plant and machinery or equipment and annual turnover
62.x: The post-2020 classification uses a composite criterion of investment in plant and machinery or equipment together with annual turnover. The earlier distinction between manufacturing and services was removed.
62.tq: Identify the exact official basis instead of a related but incorrect indicator.
xs: Since 2020, MSMEs are classed on **investment in plant and machinery or equipment AND annual turnover** — option **(4)** is correct.
Land, employees, power use, profit and exports are not criteria.
xa: This **composite** criterion was asked in **APPSC-GS 2024**.
AP follows the same definition (**APSES 2024-25**).
2020 memory aid: investment **1-10-50**, turnover **5-50-250** (₹ crore).

62.s: Under the 2020 notification, an enterprise with investment of ₹8 crore and annual turnover of ₹40 crore falls under which category?
62.x: Under the 2020 limits, a small enterprise could have investment up to ₹10 crore and turnover up to ₹50 crore. The given enterprise falls within both limits.
62.tq: Apply both limbs of the composite criterion rather than using investment alone.
xs: With **₹8 crore** investment and **₹40 crore** turnover, the unit is a **Small enterprise** — option **(2)** is correct.
Small = investment up to **₹10 crore** and turnover up to **₹50 crore**; it exceeds the micro limits of **₹1 crore / ₹5 crore**.
xa: Medium (2020): **₹50 crore** investment / **₹250 crore** turnover.
⚠ From **1 April 2025**, small = **₹25 crore / ₹100 crore**.

62.s: From 1 April 2025, what are the investment and turnover limits of a small enterprise?
62.x: The revised limits for a small enterprise are ₹25 crore investment and ₹100 crore turnover (micro ₹2.5/10 crore, medium ₹125/500 crore).
xa: These came in **Budget 2025-26**.
⚠ The **2020** limits (1-10-50 / 5-50-250) are the earlier ones, still used by the AP Survey **2024-25**.

62.s: Under the 2020 notification, what were the investment and turnover limits of a micro enterprise?
62.x: In 2020 micro meant investment up to ₹1 crore and turnover up to ₹5 crore; ₹2.5/10 crore applies from 2025.

62.s: From 1 April 2025, what are the investment and turnover limits of a medium enterprise?
62.x: From 2025 medium means ₹125 crore investment and ₹500 crore turnover.

62.s: From 1 April 2025, what are the investment and turnover limits of a micro enterprise?
62.x: The limits raised from 1 April 2025 make a micro unit one with investment up to ₹2.5 crore and turnover up to ₹10 crore.

62.s:
Consider the following statements about the MSME limits in force from 1 April 2025:
1. A micro enterprise may invest up to ₹2.5 crore.
2. The turnover ceiling of a micro enterprise is ₹15 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
62.x: The micro investment limit is ₹2.5 crore; the turnover ceiling is ₹10 crore, not ₹15 crore.

62.s: The section in the society in India which is considered to be affected considerably by the globalization process and WTO policies is
62.x: Globalisation and WTO rules (cheap imports, dereservation) hit small-scale industrialists and businessmen hardest.

62.s: For a developing country like India small scale and cottage industries should be encouraged primarily because they :
62.x: Small and cottage industries are encouraged mainly because they are labour-intensive and generate large employment.

62.s: The contribution of India's small scale sector to the gross turnover in the manufacturing sector since 1992 has been of the order of :
62.x: The small-scale sector contributed about 40% of the gross turnover of manufacturing in the 1990s.

62.s: Small Scale and Cottage Industries are important, because :
62.x: Small and cottage industries matter mainly because they provide more employment.

62.s: Which one of the following is not correct in the context of industrial clusters development in India?
o: Industrial clusters play an important role for the MSME participants in their inclusiveness, technology absorption and efficiency improvement.
Industrial clusters are visible in traditional handloom, handicrafts and modern SMC.
Industrial cluster programmes in India are administered by various ministries.
Industrial clusters lead to promotion of monopoly in the market.
62.x: Industrial clusters help MSMEs, are found in handloom, handicrafts and modern SMEs, and are run by several ministries; they do not promote monopoly.

62.s: Which one of the following is not the problem of Small Scale Industries (SSIs) ?
62.x: Strikes and lockouts are a problem of large industries; finance, marketing and raw materials are SSI problems.

62.s: Which of the following is a problem of small scale industries?
62.x: Lack of capital, marketing experience and raw material are all problems of small-scale industries.

62.s: Which of the following explains the role of small industries in the Indian economy?
o: They mainly reduce agricultural employment without affecting regional development
They are labour-intensive, require relatively little capital and help disperse industries to rural and semi-urban areas
They depend exclusively on imported technology and raw materials
They are capital-intensive and promote industrial concentration in metropolitan areas
62.x: Small industries are labour-intensive, require little capital and help disperse industrial activity to rural and semi-urban areas.
62.tq: Identify the option combining the core employment, capital and dispersal functions.
xs: Small industries are **labour-intensive**, need **little capital** and **disperse** industry to **rural and semi-urban** areas — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (4) is the reverse: they **reduce** concentration and regional imbalance.
xa: They also spread ownership of wealth and **reduce concentration of economic power**.
They have been a priority since the **First Plan**.

62.s: Small-scale industries have been treated as a priority in India since which Plan?
62.x: Small-scale industries have been a policy priority since the First Five-Year Plan.
62.tq: Use direct plan-period recall for a policy-origin question.
xs: Small industries have been a priority since the **First Plan** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Karve Committee (1955)** then planned village and small industries for the **Second Plan**.
xa: **IPR 1948** listed their handicaps: raw materials, finance, marketing, technology.
MSMEs are the second-largest employer after **agriculture**.

62.s: As per the latest Union-level figures, MSMEs account for about what share of India's exports?
62.x: MSMEs contribute about 41 per cent of exports; 31 per cent is their GDP share and 36 per cent their manufacturing-output share.

62.s: What proportion of Udyam registrations is accounted for by micro units?
62.x: Micro units account for 95.88 per cent of Udyam registrations.
62.tq: Use exact percentage recall for a composition question.
xs: **Micro units** are **95.88%** of Udyam registrations — option **(3)** is correct.
**Udyam Registration (2020)** is a free, paperless, **self-declaration** portal.
xa: **6.63 crore** MSMEs registered on Udyam (**1 July 2020 – 31 July 2025**).
These include **2.72 crore** informal micro enterprises.
**46.7 lakh+** are women-owned (Aug 2025).

62.s: How many Udyam registrations were made between 1 July 2020 and 31 July 2025?
62.x: Udyam had 6.63 crore registrations, including 2.72 crore informal micro units.

62.s: Outstanding MSME credit in India stands at about:
62.x: Outstanding MSME credit is ₹38.35 lakh crore, up from ₹10 lakh crore in 2014-15.

62.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the role of small and cottage industries?
o: They disperse industry to rural and semi-urban areas
They need large capital per worker
They reduce concentration of economic power
62.x: Small industries are labour-intensive and need little capital; they disperse industry and reduce concentration of economic power.

62.s: What is the share of MSMEs in India's GDP as per the latest Union-level figures?
62.x: MSMEs contribute about 31% of GDP, 36% of manufacturing output and 41% of exports.

62.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. MSMEs account for about 36 per cent of India's manufacturing output.
2. MSMEs account for about 41 per cent of India's exports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
62.x: Both are correct: MSMEs give about 36% of manufacturing output and 41% of exports.

62.s: What handicaps of small industries did the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 identify?
o: Raw materials, finance, marketing and technology
62.x: IPR 1948 identified difficulties relating to raw materials, finance, marketing and technology.
xa: Today's problems still include a **credit gap**, **obsolete technology** and **weak marketing**.
Others: **delayed payments**, compliance burden, **skill deficit**.

62.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a major problem faced by MSMEs?
o: Excessive access to low-cost collateral-free credit
62.x: The identified problems include obsolete technology, weak marketing and exports, compliance burden, skill deficit and costly or inadequate credit; excessive access to cheap credit is not a problem listed here.
62.tq: Use the ‘not a problem’ format to separate a real constraint from its opposite.
xs: **Excessive access to low-cost collateral-free credit** is not a problem — option **(1)** is the answer.
The real issue is a **credit gap**: little collateral and **costly credit**.
**Weak marketing and exports**, **skill deficit** and **obsolete technology** are listed problems.
xa: Other problems: **delayed payments** and **compliance burden**.
**CGTMSE** gives **collateral-free credit guarantee** cover.

62.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
62.x: MSME Samadhaan was introduced in 2017 to address delayed payments. Udyam dates from 2020, RAMP is World Bank-backed, and PM Vishwakarma covers 18 trades.
62.tq: Check the scheme, objective and year together to catch cross-swapped features.
xs: **MSME Samadhaan — delayed payments — 2017** is correctly matched — option **(2)**.
**RAMP** is World Bank-backed; **PM Vishwakarma** covers **18** trades; **Udyam** dates to **2020**.
xa: Samadhaan takes cases under the MSMED Act's **45-day** rule.
It has over **2.56 lakh** cases worth **₹55,244 crore**.

62.s: SSIs mainly suffer from a shortage of which of the following?
62.x: Shortage of working capital is the main SSI problem.

62.s: What does the MSME Samadhaan portal (2017) deal with?
62.x: MSME Samadhaan (2017) handles delayed payments: 2.56 lakh+ cases worth ₹55,244 crore.

62.s: For whom does the MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026 make settlement of MSME invoices through TReDS mandatory?
62.x: The MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026 makes TReDS settlement mandatory for CPSEs.
xa: It also provides a **National Digital Platform** for registration and additional **State MSEFCs**.
The parent **MSMED Act** came into force on **2 October 2006**; Bill introduced **12 May 2005**.
Under **Chapter V**, buyers must pay within **45 days**, else compound interest at **3 times the RBI bank rate** (**Sec. 16**).

62.s: Disputes relating to delayed payments to micro and small enterprises are referred to which body?
62.x: Disputes concerning delayed payments are referred to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council.
62.tq: Identify the specialised statutory forum rather than a general commercial or financial institution.
xs: Delayed-payment disputes go to the **MSE Facilitation Council** — option **(2)** is correct.
**SFCs** are state-level term lenders, not dispute bodies.
xa: The **MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026** adds more State **MSEFCs**.
Samadhaan cases exceed **2.56 lakh**, worth **₹55,244 crore**.

62.s: Under Chapter V of the MSMED Act, within how many days must a buyer pay an MSE supplier?
62.x: Chapter V requires payment within 45 days, beyond which compound interest at three times the RBI bank rate is payable.
xa: This is **Sec. 16** of the MSMED Act.
Disputes go to the **MSE Facilitation Council**.
**MSME Samadhaan** (**2017**) takes cases under the **45-day** rule.

62.s: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order, 2012, central ministries and CPSEs are required to procure what minimum share of their annual procurement from MSEs?
62.x: The mandatory procurement share from MSEs is 25 per cent; it was raised from 20 per cent in 2018.
62.tq: Test the current mandatory share against its earlier level.
xs: Central ministries and CPSEs must buy at least **25 per cent** of annual procurement from MSEs — so option **(3)** is correct.
**20 per cent** was the earlier mandate, raised to 25% in **2018**.
xa: Sub-targets: **4%** from **SC/ST-owned** MSEs and **3%** from **women-owned** MSEs.
**Achieved** in FY26 (to **1 Dec 2025**): **44.76%**, above the mandate.
**GeM:** **Rs 18.4 lakh crore** GMV; **11 lakh+** MSEs.

62.s: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, what is the sub-target for procurement from women-owned MSEs?
62.x: The sub-targets are 3 per cent from women-owned MSEs and 4 per cent from SC/ST-owned MSEs.
xa: Overall mandate: **25%** of annual procurement (raised from **20%** in **2018**).
Order issued as the **Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order, 2012**.
Actual MSE procurement reached **44.76%** in FY26.

62.s: If a buyer delays payment to an MSE supplier, at what rate must it pay compound interest?
o: Three times the RBI bank rate
Four times the RBI bank rate
62.x: Section 16 of the MSMED Act prescribes compound interest at 3 times the RBI bank rate.

62.s: Under the Public Procurement Policy, what is the sub-target for SC/ST-owned MSEs?
62.x: The sub-targets are 4% for SC/ST-owned and 3% for women-owned MSEs.

62.s: From what level was the procurement target from MSEs raised to 25% in 2018?
62.x: Ministries and CPSEs must buy 25% from MSEs, raised from 20% in 2018.

Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false

63.tq: Ask whether lower costs explain competitiveness.

Lower technology and capital-equipment costs boost domestic manufacturing competitiveness. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
xs: Both A and R are true, and **R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Liberalisation instruments — **de-licensing**, **import deregulation**, **lower import duty on capital goods** — **lower the cost of technology and capital equipment**.
That cost cut is what **boosts domestic manufacturing competitiveness** — R explains A.

65.s: After the merger of Air India and Indian Airlines, the New entity is now known as :
65.x: Air India and Indian Airlines merged in 2007 to form a single entity called Air India.

65.s: What is the sale of government equity in public sector enterprises known as?
65.x: Selling government equity is disinvestment; liberalisation is removal of licences, quotas and controls.
xa: **Privatisation** = transfer of **ownership and management control** to the private sector.
**Monetisation** leases assets; **ownership stays with government**.
**Strategic sale** = block of shares (usually **50%+**) plus transfer of management control.

65.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes disinvestment from privatisation?
o: Disinvestment always transfers management control; privatisation may retain government control
Both always transfer management control to the private sector
Disinvestment reduces government equity; privatisation transfers ownership and management control to the private sector
Privatisation reduces equity without transfer of control; disinvestment transfers ownership
65.x: Disinvestment is a reduction of government equity, possibly with government retaining control; privatisation transfers ownership and management control to the private sector.
xa: **Strategic sale**: a block of shares (usually **50%+**) plus transfer of management control.
**Complete privatisation**: **100%** sold — the most comprehensive mode.
⚠ **Monetisation** leases assets; disinvestment sells equity permanently.

65.s: A government retains more than 51 per cent equity and control in a public sector enterprise while selling a part of its holding. What is this called?
65.x: Under minority disinvestment, the government retains more than 51 per cent ownership and control. Majority disinvestment transfers control while retaining a minority stake.
65.tq: Apply the percentage and control test to distinguish minority and majority disinvestment.
xs: Keeping **more than 51%** and control while selling part is **minority disinvestment** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Majority disinvestment** transfers control but keeps a minority stake; **complete privatisation** sells **100%**.
xa: **Strategic sale** = block of shares (usually **50%+**) + transfer of management control.
The first round (**1991-92**) sold minority stakes in **31 PSUs**.
**Economic Survey 2025-26** proposes letting the stake in listed CPSEs fall to **26%** while keeping "Government company" status.

65.s: What does a strategic sale of a public sector enterprise generally involve?
o: Sale of a block of shares, usually 50% or more, with transfer of management control
Sale of a minority stake with the government retaining control
Leasing assets for a fixed period with ownership retained by the government
Listing shares through an IPO without any change in management
65.x: A strategic sale normally involves a block of shares, usually 50% or more, along with transfer of management control to a strategic partner.
xa: The **Disinvestment Commission (1996)** recommended strategic sales.
First strategic sales came in **1999-2004**.
Since **2016**, in-principle approval for strategic sale of **36 CPSEs**; **13 completed**.

65.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or concern relating to disinvestment?
o: Automatic improvement in public ownership of strategic assets
National-security concerns in oil, defence and transport
65.x: The identified concerns include undervaluation, loss of dividend income and national-security risks in sectors such as oil, defence and transport. Automatic improvement in public ownership is not a criticism of disinvestment.
65.tq: Find the option that is inconsistent with the stated criticism of the policy.
xs: **Automatic improvement in public ownership** is not a concern — option **(2)** is the answer; disinvestment reduces public ownership.
Listed concerns: **undervaluation**, **loss of dividend income**, **national-security** concerns in **oil, defence, transport**.
xa: Main criticism: "**selling the family silver**" to fill the **fiscal deficit**.
**Risk of private monopolies** and **union resistance** are also debated.
**New PSE Policy 2021** keeps a "**bare minimum**" **1-4** CPSEs in **4** strategic sectors.

65.s: Why is the expression “selling the family silver” used in criticism of disinvestment?
o: all public assets are sold below their book value in every transaction
the proceeds are used to bridge the fiscal deficit instead of building assets
disinvestment necessarily increases dividend income for the government
the proceeds are exclusively invested in new public enterprises
65.x: The expression criticises the use of disinvestment proceeds to bridge the fiscal deficit rather than to create or build assets.
65.tq: Interpret an idiomatic expression through the policy criticism it represents.
xs: "**Selling the family silver**" criticises using **proceeds to bridge the fiscal deficit instead of building assets** — option **(2)** is correct.
Disinvestment actually means **loss of dividend income**, not more.
xa: Other concerns: **undervaluation** of PSU assets; **national-security** concerns in oil, defence, transport.
Debates also note **union resistance** and the **risk of private monopolies**.
NIF rule: proceeds credited, **only income** used.

65.s: Which mode is considered the most comprehensive mode of privatisation?
65.x: Complete privatisation, selling 100%, is the most comprehensive mode.

65.x: Liberalisation removes licences, quotas and controls; it involves no sale.

65.s: Which of the following is a disinvestment instrument used by DIPAM?

**LIC IPO** (**17 May 2022**) was the biggest IPO then, with about **73 lakh** applications.

65.x: SLR, CRR and repo are monetary tools, not disinvestment methods.

65.s: Under the Competition Act, 2002, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
