123.s: What is the loan amount distributed to the SHG Women through "Stree Nidhi" during the year 2018-19?
123.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
123.x: Printed key Rs 4,313 crore of Stree Nidhi loans to SHG women in 2018-19; not re-checked (Rs 21,123.71 crore lent in all, 2011-2024).

123.s: What is the name of the community based micro finance organization floated by Mandal Samakhyas along with the Government of Andhra Pradesh?
123.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
123.x: Stree Nidhi is the community-based micro-finance body floated by the Mandal Samakhyas with GoAP (2011). Velugu was the poverty programme; Naandi is an NGO.

123.s: What do SHG members often lack, which makes it hard for them to scale up beyond linkage loans?
123.x: Members often lack individual CIBIL credit histories needed to scale up, and linkage loans are seen as too small for expansion.
xa: AP leads SHG-bank linkage: **36%** share, **99.66%** recovery (**2024-25**).
**MEPMA** SHG bank linkage up to **Rs 20 lakh**.

123.s: Which State has a 36% share in SHG-bank linkage and is described as a leading State in this area?
123.x: Andhra Pradesh leads SHG-bank linkage with a stated share of 36%.
123.tq: Match the State with its distinctive sectoral share.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** — **first place**, **36%** national share — option **(4)**.
Its recovery rate is **99.66%** (**2024-25**).
xa: **Stree Nidhi** = SHG credit federation.
Criticism: loans **too small**; no individual **CIBIL** histories.

123.s: What is the full form of SERP?
o: Society for Empowerment of Rural Poor
State Employment and Rural Prosperity Mission
Society for Eradication of Rural Penury
Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty
123.x: SERP is the Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty, which runs Velugu/Indira Kranthi Patham.

123.s: In which year was SERP in Andhra Pradesh registered?
123.x: SERP was registered in 2000; it was split into AP SERP and TG SERP after 2014.

123.s: In which year was DWCRA (Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas) launched?
123.x: DWCRA was launched in September 1982 with Centre:State funding of 75:25.

123.s: With whose support does SERP run Velugu (Indira Kranthi Patham) in Andhra Pradesh?
123.x: SERP runs Velugu/Indira Kranthi Patham with World Bank support.

123.s: What was the recovery rate of SHG-bank linkage loans in Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
123.x: AP leads India in SHG-bank linkage, with a 36% national share and 99.66% recovery in 2024-25.

123.s: In what ratio was DWCRA funded by the Centre and the State?
123.x: DWCRA, launched in September 1982, was funded by the Centre and the State in the ratio 75:25.

123.s: What is Stree Nidhi in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Credit cooperative federation promoted with SHG federations
123.x: Stree Nidhi is a credit cooperative federation promoted with SHG federations.
xa: **MEPMA** serves urban SHGs.
AP leads SHG-bank linkage: **36%** national share, **99.66%** recovery.

123.s: What is the full form of MEPMA?
o: Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas
Municipal Employment and Poverty Management Authority
Mission for Economic Planning in Metropolitan Areas
Mission for Empowerment of Panchayats and Municipal Administration
123.x: MEPMA means Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas and serves urban SHGs.
123.tq: Discriminate between similar expansions of the acronym.
xs: **MEPMA** = **Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas** — option **(1)**.
It serves **urban SHGs**.
xa: **9,018** slum-level federations; **206** town/city federations; **24** Zilla Samakhyas.
Revolving fund to SHGs: **Rs 52.60 crore**.

123.s: Up to what amount is SHG bank linkage permitted under the MEPMA self-employment programme?
123.x: MEPMA permits SHG bank linkage up to Rs 20 lakh; individual loans range from Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh and group loans up to Rs 10 lakh.
xa: MEPMA = **Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas**.
Revolving fund: **Rs 52.60 crore**.

123.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Stree Nidhi – Credit to SHG members
123.x: MEPMA (Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas) works with urban SHGs; SERP works in rural areas.

123.s: What is the range of individual loans to members under MEPMA?
123.x: MEPMA individual loans are Rs 50,000-2 lakh; group loans go up to Rs 10 lakh and SHG bank linkage up to Rs 20 lakh.

123.s: For whom is the Pattabhi Sitaramayya-Self Business Group (PS-SBG) scheme of Andhra Bank meant?
123.x: Andhra Bank launched PS-SBG to help rural women start their own businesses.

123.s: What is the main service provided by Stree Nidhi to SHG members in Andhra Pradesh?
123.x: Stree Nidhi is a credit cooperative federation that gives timely, affordable credit to SHG members.

123.s: Which organisation in Andhra Pradesh works with self-help groups of the urban poor in municipal areas?
123.x: MEPMA (Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas) handles urban SHGs; SERP works in rural areas.

123.s: NABARD's Primary role is:
o: To provide term loans to state co-operative banks
To assist state government for share capital contribution
To act as a re-finance institution
123.x: NABARD gives term loans (refinance) to State Cooperative Banks, lends to State Governments for their share-capital contribution to cooperatives, and works mainly as a refinance institution - so all of the above.

123.s: With regard to NABARD, which of the following statements is not true?
o: it is an apex and refinancing institution
it does not directly provide short-term credit to the needy farmers
it gives long-term loans to state governments to enable them to strengthen the share capital of cooperative credit societies
it has the responsibility to inspect RRBs, and co-operative banks including primary co-operative societies
123.x: NABARD inspects RRBs and State and District Central Cooperative Banks, but not primary cooperative societies, which are inspected by the Registrar or DCCBs - so option 4 is untrue. NABARD does not lend short-term credit directly to farmers, so option 2 is true.

123.s: NABARD was setup in 1982 on the recommendation of
123.x: NABARD was set up on the recommendation of CRAFICARD (Committee to Review Arrangements for Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural Development), chaired by B. Sivaraman. The Narasimham committees dealt with RRBs and banking reform.

123.s: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was established on the recommendation of which of the following Committee?
123.x: NABARD (12 July 1982) was set up on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee (CRAFICARD). Narasimham committees dealt with RRBs (1975) and banking reform (1991).

123.s: By whom has NABARD been fully owned since 2019?
123.x: Since 2019 NABARD is fully owned by the Government of India; it is headquartered in Mumbai and started with Rs 100 crore.
xa: It took over RBI's **ACD** and **RPCC** + the **ARDC**.
Recommended by the **B. Sivaraman Committee (CRAFICARD)**.

123.s: In which year was the Kisan Credit Card, a NABARD model scheme based on the R.V. Gupta Committee, introduced?
123.x: The KCC was introduced in 1998 as a NABARD model scheme based on the R.V. Gupta Committee.
xa: RBI revised **KCC Directions**: **19 Jun 2026**, for loans from **1 Jan 2027**.
Maximum tenure now **6 years** (earlier **5**).

123.s: In which year was the NABARD Act passed?
123.x: The NABARD Act was passed in 1981 and NABARD was set up in 1982, the same year as the EXIM Bank.
n: NABARD was established through the NABARD Act, 1981. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
EXIM Bank was set up in 1982. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
xa: NABARD's initial corpus was **Rs 100 crore**.
NABARD came from the **B. Sivaraman Committee (CRAFICARD)**.
**SIDBI** followed on **April 2, 1990**.

123.s: On its establishment, NABARD took over the whole of which body, besides RBI's ACD and RPCC?
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India
123.x: NABARD took over RBI's Agricultural Credit Department and Rural Planning and Credit Cell and the whole of the ARDC.
xa: **Fully Government-owned since 2019**.
HQ **Mumbai**.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about the chronology of rural credit institutions:
1. Regional Rural Banks (1975) came before NABARD (1982).
2. The SHG–Bank Linkage Programme (1992–93) came before NABARD.
3. The Kisan Credit Card (1998) came after the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: The order is RRBs (1975), NABARD (1982), SHG–Bank Linkage (1992–93) and KCC (1998), so statement 2 is wrong.
n: NABARD was established on 12 July 1982. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-24]
Regional Rural Banks were established in 1975. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-24]
The SHG–Bank Linkage Programme was established in 1992–93. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-24]
The Kisan Credit Card Plan was established in 1998. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-24]

123.s: Where is the headquarters of NABARD?
123.x: NABARD, set up on 12 July 1982, has its headquarters in Mumbai.

123.s: On the recommendation of which committee was NABARD set up?
123.x: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee (CRAFICARD).

123.s: When was the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) set up?
123.x: SIDBI, the principal institution for MSMEs, was set up on 2 April 1990.

123.s: With what initial capital did NABARD begin in 1982?
123.x: NABARD began with Rs 100 crore; Rs 2,000 crore was the starting corpus of RIDF.

123.s: Which of the following was set up in 1982, the same year as NABARD?
123.x: EXIM Bank was set up in 1982 like NABARD; SIDBI came in 1990 and RRBs in 1975.

123.s: The scheme for which land development package is designed for the development of land distributed to the poor is
123.x: Indira Prabha (2004) is the integrated land development scheme for land assigned to the poor. The other names are not such schemes.

123.s: The programme initiated by the State government with the support of NABARD for land development is
123.x: Indira Prabha is the AP land development programme taken up with NABARD support. Indira Kranti is the SHG/poverty programme; Janmabhoomi is about people's participation.

123.s: The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) has been created under ;
123.x: The Government of India created the RIDF in NABARD in 1995-96 with a corpus of Rs 2,000 crore.

123.s: The nodal agency for implementing the ‘Rural Infrastructure Development Fund Programmes’ is :
123.x: NABARD is the nodal agency for the RIDF, created in NABARD in 1995-96.

123.s: Which of the following about the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) is NOT correct?
123.x: RIDF began in 1995–96 with an initial corpus of ₹2,000 crore, not ₹20,000 crore.
n: The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund was created in 1995–96. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
The initial corpus of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund was ₹2,000 crore. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
Agriculture and related sectors are broad areas of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
The social sector is a broad area of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
Rural connectivity is a broad area of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
xa: RIDF is **administered by NABARD**, its **nodal agency**.
Examples: **rural roads**, **rural water supply**, **rural electrification**.
In AP, **68** lift irrigation schemes were modernised at **Rs 74.22 crore** under RIDF.

123.s: Under the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), rural drinking water supply falls under which category?
123.x: Rural drinking water is under the social sector; rural roads fall under rural connectivity and minor irrigation under agriculture and related sectors.
n: The initial corpus of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund was ₹2,000 crore. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
Agriculture and related sectors are broad areas of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
The social sector is a broad area of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
Rural connectivity is a broad area of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
Rural roads are an example of the areas covered by the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
Rural water supply is an example of the areas covered by the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
Rural electrification is an example of the areas covered by the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]

123.s: Which of the following NABARD funds is wrongly matched with its purpose?
o: LTIF – State share of ongoing PMKSY irrigation projects
Warehouse Infrastructure Fund – Rural infrastructure loans to States
123.x: The Warehouse Infrastructure Fund supports scientific storage and APMC facilities; rural infrastructure loans to States come from RIDF.
xa: **AP is among 8 states** funded by the Micro Irrigation Fund.
Warehouse Infrastructure Fund dates from **2013-14**.

123.s: To which fund does money from the sale of Government shares (disinvestment) go?
123.x: Disinvestment proceeds go to the NIF, not to RIDF.

123.s: What was the initial corpus of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), created in 1995-96?
123.x: RIDF began in 1995-96 with Rs 2,000 crore and is administered by NABARD; disinvestment proceeds go to the NIF, not RIDF.
n: The purpose of the National Investment Fund is to channelise proceeds from the disinvestment of Central Public Sector Enterprises. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund was created in 1995–96. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
The initial corpus of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund was ₹2,000 crore. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund is administered by NABARD. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
xa: Broad areas: **agriculture**, **social sector**, **rural connectivity**.
**Indira Prabha** is a State-NABARD programme for **land development**.
**Warehouse Infrastructure Fund** (**2013-14**) supports scientific storage.

123.s: Which programme was taken up in Andhra Pradesh with NABARD support for land development?
123.x: Indira Prabha was AP's land development programme supported by NABARD.

123.s: What was the purpose of the Indira Prabha programme in Andhra Pradesh?
123.x: Indira Prabha aimed at developing the lands of the poor with NABARD support.

123.s: How many lift irrigation schemes in Andhra Pradesh were modernised under RIDF in 2024-25 to stabilise 1.03 lakh acres?
123.x: In 2024-25, 68 lift irrigation schemes were modernised at Rs 74.22 crore to stabilise 1.03 lakh acres.

123.s: Which sector receives the largest share of RIDF loans to States?
123.x: Irrigation gets about 30% of RIDF loans, ahead of roads (26%) and the social sector (21%).

123.s: The major source of Agricultural Credit in Andhra Pradesh State during the last decade is
123.x: Commercial banks have been the major source of institutional farm credit in AP, as in India; cooperatives gave about one-fifth of crop loans (2007-08).

123.s: In 2007-08, in Andhra Pradesh nearly one fifth of the total crop loans to farmers is provided by
123.x: In 2007-08 cooperative credit societies gave about one-fifth of AP's crop loans, commercial banks most of the rest.

123.s: Rural Banks were instituted according to the recommendations of
123.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Horticulture
123.x:
Most books and keys: Narasimham Committee. Strictly: the 1975 Working Group on Rural Banks chaired by M. Narasimham, not the 1991 Narasimham Committee on the financial system (NextGen Indian Economy - APPSC 07 p.8).
Regional Rural Banks (2 Oct 1975) came on the recommendation of the Working Group on Rural Banks chaired by M. Narasimham; Sivaraman's committee led to NABARD.

123.s: Into which bank was Andhra Bank, founded by Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Machilipatnam in 1923, merged in 2020?
123.x: Andhra Bank merged into Union Bank of India on 1 April 2020.
xa: Andhra Bank launched the **PS-SBG** scheme for rural women.
NABARD was set up in **1982**, HQ **Mumbai**.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about Regional Rural Banks (RRBs):
1. RRBs were established on 2 October 1975.
2. Prathama Bank was the first RRB.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: Both are correct: RRBs began on 2 October 1975, and Prathama Bank (Moradabad) was the first RRB.
n: Regional Rural Banks were established on October 2, 1975. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
Prathama Bank was the first Regional Rural Bank. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
Regional Rural Banks were established in 1975. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
Regional Rural Banks were established following the recommendations of the Narasimham Working Group. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]

123.s: Which committee's 1991 report began banking-sector reforms in India?
123.x: The Narasimham Committee I (1991) launched banking reforms through its recommendations to admit new private banks and deregulate interest rates.
n: The Narasimham Committee I report kicked off economic liberalisation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The Narasimham Committee I report led to the entry of private banks. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The Narasimham Committee I report led to the deregulation of interest rates. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
xa: **RRBs** came earlier, on the **Narasimham Working Group**'s advice (**1975**).
**NABARD** (**1982**) and **SIDBI** (**1990**) preceded the 1991 report.
**Andhra Bank** was founded by **Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya**.

123.s: On whose recommendation were Regional Rural Banks set up?
123.x: RRBs (1975) came from the Narasimham Working Group; Sivaraman led to NABARD and R.V. Gupta to KCC.

123.s: Who founded Andhra Bank at Machilipatnam in 1923?
123.x: Andhra Bank was founded by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Machilipatnam in 1923.

123.s: Nationally, scheduled commercial banks provide about what share of formal farm credit?
123.x: Scheduled commercial banks provide over 70% of formal farm credit nationally.
xa: Cooperatives (**PACS-DCCB-SCB**) = short-term; **ARDBs** = long-term.
National farm credit **2024-25**: **Rs 28.69 lakh crore** vs **Rs 27.50 lakh crore** target (**104%**).

123.s: The lack of which of the following mainly keeps tenant, tribal, women and oral-lessee farmers in Andhra Pradesh out of formal credit?
123.x: Formal lending generally requires land records, which many such farmers do not possess.
xa: ACP **2025-26**: **Rs 1,490 crore** to **tenant farmers**.
The **Modified Interest Subvention Scheme** covers tenant farmers and **SHGs** too.

123.s: Which of the following is NOT an institutional source of agricultural finance for farmers in Andhra Pradesh?
123.x: Commercial banks, RRBs and PACS are institutional sources; informal moneylenders are not.
xa: Other formal sources: **SHGs/JLGs**, microfinance, **KCC**.
Nationally, scheduled commercial banks give **over 70%** of formal farm credit.
NABARD Guntur study: formal interest rates about **2.5-10%**.

123.s: Which institutions mainly provide long-term agricultural credit in India's cooperative credit structure?
123.x: ARDBs (Agriculture and Rural Development Banks) provide long-term credit, whereas the PACS-DCCB-State Cooperative Bank chain mainly provides short-term credit.

123.s: What is the maximum period of a short-term agricultural loan?
123.x: Short-term loans run up to 1 year, with a maximum of 15 months; longer loans are medium- or long-term.

123.s: From which date were Andhra Pradesh's four RRBs merged into Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank under 'One State, One RRB'?
123.x: The four AP RRBs were amalgamated into Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank from 1 May 2025.

123.s: Which is the sponsor bank of Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank?
123.x: Union Bank of India sponsors the single AP RRB, Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank.

123.s: Which of the following was NOT among the RRBs merged into Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank in 2025?
123.x: Prathama Bank (Moradabad) was India's first RRB; the four merged were Chaitanya Godavari, Andhra Pragathi, Saptagiri and AP Grameena Vikas Bank.

123.s: After the 'One State, One RRB' amalgamation, to how many did the number of RRBs in India fall from 43?
123.x: RRBs in India fell from 43 to 28.

123.s: Under the YSR Zero Interest Crop scheme launched by the Andhra Pradesh government on 20 April 2021, farmers were provided crop loans up to______during the rabi season.
123.x: The 20 April 2021 payout of the YSR Zero Interest Crop Loan scheme covered rabi crop loans up to Rs 1 lakh repaid on time.

123.s: "Pavala Vaddi" Scheme covers?
o: Retail loans of more than Rs 1 lakh and upto Rs 3 lakhs
All bank loans taken by BPL cardholders
Crop loans of more than Rs 1 lakh and upto Rs 3 lakhs
123.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
123.x: In AP crop loans up to Rs 1 lakh were interest-free (Vaddi Leni Runalu), while Pavala Vaddi (3%, "quarter-rupee" interest) covered crop loans above Rs 1 lakh and up to Rs 3 lakh repaid on time.

123.s: Up to what amount were rabi crop loans covered at the 20 April 2021 payout of the YSR Zero Interest Crop Loan scheme?
123.x: The scheme covered rabi crop loans up to Rs 1 lakh for farmers who repaid on time, with the State bearing the interest.
xa: ⚠ State scheme: **Rs 1 lakh** at **zero**; central scheme: **Rs 3 lakh** at **4%**.
The central scheme is run by **RBI** and **NABARD**.

123.s: At what interest rate are short-term crop loans up to Rs 3 lakh available to prompt repayers under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme?
123.x: Short-term crop loans up to Rs 3 lakh are available at 4% for prompt repayers.
xa: Implemented by **RBI** and **NABARD**.
Covers farmers, **tenant farmers** and **SHGs** (**2026**).

123.s:
Consider the following statements about the revised Kisan Credit Card Directions issued by the RBI on 19 June 2026:
1. They apply to loans from 1 January 2027.
2. They raise the maximum KCC tenure to six years.
3. The earlier maximum KCC tenure was three years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: The directions apply from 1 January 2027 and raise the maximum tenure to six years; the earlier maximum was five years, not three.

123.s: In 2024–25, the disbursement of farm credit in India was approximately what percentage of the target?
123.x: Farm credit disbursement was Rs 28.69 lakh crore against a target of Rs 27.50 lakh crore, amounting to 104 per cent of the target.
123.tq: Calculate the performance ratio from the reported target and achievement figures.
xs: Farm credit was **104 per cent** of target — option **(3)**.
**Rs 28.69 lakh crore** disbursed vs **Rs 27.50 lakh crore** target (**2024-25**).
xa: AP ACP **2025-26**: **Rs 2.96 lakh crore** to agriculture + allied.
Commercial banks give **over 70%** of formal farm credit.

123.s:
Consider the following statements about the YSR Zero Interest Crop Loan scheme:
1. It covers crop loans up to Rs 1 lakh repaid on time.
2. The State Government pays the interest.
3. It gives loans up to Rs 3 lakh at 4%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
123.x: The scheme covers loans up to Rs 1 lakh repaid on time with the State paying interest; Rs 3 lakh at 4% is the central Modified Interest Subvention Scheme.

123.s: Who bears the interest on eligible loans under the YSR Zero Interest Crop Loan scheme?
123.x: The State pays the interest on crop loans up to Rs 1 lakh repaid on time.

130.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, on whom do loans re-lent for projects confined to only one successor State devolve?

The State having the larger population
Both successor States in the population ratio

xs: They devolve on **the State in which the project is located** — option **(2)** (**Section 54**, APRA 2014).
Other Public Debt & Public Account liabilities are split by **population ratio**.
xa: **Section 55**: floating loans for one State stay with it; others split by population ratio.

130.s: Since Andhra Pradesh continues to run a primary deficit, its borrowing is used to meet:

130.s: What does the 'golden rule' of public borrowing say borrowing should generally be used for?
130.x: The golden rule states that borrowing should be undertaken only for creating capital assets, rather than for routine revenue expenditure.
130.tq: Apply the fiscal principle to distinguish capital creation from current spending.
xs: The golden rule: borrow only for **capital assets** — option **(1)**: creating capital assets.
Financing revenue spending or interest breaks the rule.
xa: AP still runs a **primary deficit** → borrowing also meets current spending.
Capex creates **productive assets**; committed spending squeezes it.
AP's ₹11,000 cr of 50-year interest-free capex loans lie outside the FD ceiling.

130.s: How are interest payments treated in the Andhra Pradesh Budget?
o: A voted item of developmental expenditure
A discretionary grant to local bodies

It is committed, **non-developmental** spending.
xa: SES 2025-26: interest crowds out developmental spending.
2026-27 BE interest: **₹37,281 cr** (16% of revenue receipts).

130.s: In what are investments of the Consolidated Sinking Fund made?

130.s: Guarantees given by the Andhra Pradesh government crystallise as liabilities only when they are:
130.x: Guarantees are contingent liabilities that crystallise if invoked; they are not part of outstanding debt before that.
xa: The **GRF** (RBI) helps States meet invoked guarantees.
Budget 2026-27 guarantees: **Rs. 1,77,328 Cr (10% of GSDP)**.
Growing reliance on **State-backed guarantees** to fund essential machinery.

130.s: Which of the following is NOT a recommendation of the Sixteenth Finance Commission?

130.s: Which of the following is a component of Tax Revenue?
130.x: Corporation tax is tax revenue. Interest, dividends and fees are non-tax revenue.
n: Tax revenue includes corporation tax. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 66-68]
Non-tax revenue includes interest receipts. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 66-68]
Non-tax revenue includes dividends and profits from public enterprises. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 66-68]
Non-tax revenue includes fees and other receipts. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 66-68]
xs: **Corporation Tax** is a component of **tax revenue** — option **(3)**.
**Tax revenue** includes **income tax**, **corporation tax**, **customs**, **union excise** and **GST**.
**Dividends and profits**, **fees** and **interest receipts** are **non-tax revenue**.
xa: **Revenue receipts** consist of **tax revenue** and **non-tax revenue**.
Non-tax revenue = receipts **not raised by taxing the public** — fines, user charges, royalties.
Royalties and departmental receipts are also non-tax revenue.
